segments.title: Theorem 1.1 statement
segments.reason: The segment is Theorem 1.1 (Seymour's second-neighborhood statement): every nonempty finite oriented graph has a vertex v with |N+(v)| ≤ |N++(v)|. The Lean `exists_goodVertex` matches each piece: `[Fintype V]` = finite, `[Nonempty V]` = nonempty, `(r : V → V → Prop)` with `(hr : IsOriented r)` = oriented graph, and `∃ v, GoodVertex r v` = has a vertex v satisfying the good-vertex property (|N+(v)| ≤ |N++(v)|). The quantifier structure (universal over the graph via free variables + hypotheses, existential over v) and direction match. This is faithful provided `GoodVertex r v` is defined as |N+(v)| ≤ |N++(v)|, which its name and the theorem's context indicate; the definition itself is outside this segment.

segments.title: Proposition 2.1 (counterexample reduction) statement
segments.reason: The NL asserts: if Theorem 1.1 has a counterexample (an oriented graph satisfying the counterexample condition), then there exists a finite nonempty oriented graph G with positive indegree at every vertex and |U|+|F²G(U)| < 2|FG(U)| for every nonempty proper subset U. The Lean `counterexample_reduction` takes hypotheses `IsOriented r` and `Counterexample r` (= the counterexample to Thm 1.1) and concludes `∃ n, 0 < n ∧ ∃ g : (Fin n × Fin (n+1)) → …, IsOriented g ∧ PositiveIndegree g ∧ StrictSubsetGrowth g`. The vertex type `Fin n × Fin (n+1)` with `0 < n` is finite (Fintype) and nonempty, matching 'finite nonempty graph'; `IsOriented g` matches 'oriented'; `PositiveIndegree g` (∀v, ∃u, g u v) matches 'every vertex has positive indegree'; and `StrictSubsetGrowth` (∀S, S.Nonempty → S ≠ univ → S.card + (image r (image r S)).card < 2*(image r S).card) matches |U|+|F²G(U)| < 2|FG(U)| over all nonempty proper subsets. Using a specific concrete vertex type is a legitimate witness for the bare existence claim, so nothing is dropped, weakened, or strengthened.

segments.title: Lemma 2.2 (subset deficit) statement
segments.reason: The segment is Lemma 2.2's statement: for a finite nonempty oriented graph D with |N⁺₁(v)|>|N⁺₂(v)| for all v, chosen with minimum order and then minimum arcs, (1) D is strongly connected, (2) every vertex has positive indegree, and (3) |F₂(S)\F(S)| < |F(S)\S| for every ∅≠S⊊V(D). The Lean captures all of this. The hypothesis |N⁺₁(v)|>|N⁺₂(v)| is `Counterexample r` (used as (secondNeighbors r v).card < (firstNeighbors r v).card for every v). The minimality choice is `exists_minimal_counterexample`, which builds s via Nat.find first on order (OrderMinimal) and then, at that order, on arc count (ArcMinimal) — exactly 'minimum order and, subject to that, minimum arcs.' Conclusion (1): `NonemptyBoundary r` states (image r S \ S).Nonempty for every nonempty proper S, which is the standard characterization of strong connectivity (every nonempty proper vertex set has an arc leaving it). Conclusion (2) is `PositiveIndegree r`. Conclusion (3) is `SubsetDeficit r`: via `subsetDeficit_of_minimal` and `deficitPotential_terminal` it gives (image r (image r S) \ image r S).card < (image r S \ S).card, i.e. |F₂(S)\F(S)| < |F(S)\S| (F = image r, F₂ = image r ∘ image r), quantified over nonempty S≠univ (∅≠S⊊V). Direction of the strict inequality and all quantifiers match.

segments.title: Lemma 2.2 proof
segments.reason: The Lean captures exactly the content of this segment's subset-deficit argument. Definitions match: deficitPotential r S T = |image r T \ ((image r S ∩ S) ∪ T)| is g(T)=|F(T)\(I∪T)| with I=F(S)∩S, E=F(S)\S. The step lemma deficitPotential_step builds Q nonempty ⊆ (F(S)\S)\T with deficitPotential(T∪Q) < deficitPotential(T) + |Q|, which is exactly inequality (5) g(T∪Q)−g(T) < |Q|. Its proof mirrors the NL: s = r minus all arcs (x,y) with x∈S, y∈E\T (deleting arcs from S to E\T); hremain/harcStrict give that ≥1 arc is deleted since every vertex of E\T receives an arc from S; minimality yields v with |N⁺₁,DT(v)|≤|N⁺₂,DT(v)| (hvGood); hcut forces v∈S and Q=F({v})∩(E\T) nonempty; hfirstCover/hfirstNewCover/hpathCover realize F²_DT({v}) ⊆ I∪T∪F(T) (eq 4); B=Q∩image r T is the newly-counted set (gain ⊆ B), C=F(Q)\(I∪T∪Q∪F(T)) is the lost set (C ⊆ N⁺₂,D(v)), and the balance identity g(T∪Q)+|B| = g(T)+|C| plus d2<d1 (hcounter v) give the strict bound — matching the chain d1−|Q| ≤ |N⁺₂,DT(v)| ≤ d2−|C|+|Q∩F(T)| and |C|−|Q∩F(T)| ≤ |Q|+d2−d1 < |Q|. deficitPotential_terminal proves g(E)=|F²(S)\F(S)| via F²(S)\F(S)=F(E)\(I∪E) (eq 3), and subsetDeficit_of_minimal iterates the step from ∅ to E (strict_deficit_of_augmentation) to conclude g(E)<|E|, i.e. |F²(S)\F(S)|<|F(S)\S|. Quantifiers, inequality directions, and the exactness of the g-change all agree. Strong connectivity (first paragraph) enters only through the NonemptyBoundary hypothesis (E=F(S)\S nonempty), which is precisely how the segment uses it ('Strong connectivity gives E≠∅'); the full strong-connectivity/in-neighbor derivation is encapsulated in the Counterexample/NonemptyBoundary hypotheses of this relevant part rather than re-proved, consistent with the segment.

segments.title: Lemma 2.3 (transitive-tournament blowup) statement
segments.reason: The segment describes the transitive-tournament blowup construction and its hypotheses. The Lean `blowup r m := fun p q => r p.1 q.1 ∨ (p.1 = q.1 ∧ p.2 < q.2)` faithfully captures this: vertices become pairs (base vertex, Fin m) — i.e. each vertex is replaced by a block of m vertices; the disjunct `p.1 = q.1 ∧ p.2 < q.2` is a transitive tournament on the m vertices within a block (the strict linear order on Fin m); the disjunct `r p.1 q.1` puts an arc from every p in block v to every q in block w exactly when v→w is an arc of D (`r v w`), in the correct direction; and since the cross-block disjunct requires `p.1 = q.1`, no other arcs exist between distinct blocks. The hypotheses on D match those used in `blowup_strictSubsetGrowth`: positive indegree (`PositiveIndegree r`), condition (3) for every nonempty proper subset (`SubsetDeficit r`), orientedness (`IsOriented r`), and m > n (`Fintype.card V < m`). The only item not separately imposed is n ≥ 1, but that is a background nondegeneracy condition, not part of the construction this segment defines, and does not alter what is asserted.

segments.title: Lemma 2.3 proof
segments.reason: The segment asserts three things about the blown-up graph G and proves them: (a) G is oriented, (b) all indegrees in G are positive, and (c) G satisfies (2), i.e. for every nonempty proper U, |U| - 2|FG(U)| + |F²G(U)| < 0. The Lean matches all three. `blowup_isOriented` gives IsOriented (blowup r m) from IsOriented r (loopless + asymmetric, correctly handling cross-block arcs and within-block Fin m order). `blowup_positiveIndegree` gives PositiveIndegree (blowup r m) from PositiveIndegree r, matching 'every vertex receives arcs from an incoming base block.' `blowup_strictSubsetGrowth` establishes StrictSubsetGrowth (blowup r m) under exactly the hypotheses the NL uses: IsOriented, PositiveIndegree, SubsetDeficit (the (3)/subset-deficit hypothesis), and Fintype.card V < m (n < m). Its conclusion, via `card_add_card_lt_twice_of_sdiff`, is U.card + (second image).card < 2*(first image).card, i.e. |U| + |F²G(U)| < 2|FG(U)|, the same inequality and direction as the NL's < 0 bound. The case split mirrors the NL: the non-full-support case (U.image fst ≠ univ) invokes the subset-deficit bound and the m-amplification (hgain/hloss/hamp capture 'two external arcs reach an F²(S)-block', boundary arcs, and the strict-inequality amplification giving the -m+n < 0 margin), and the full-support case (S = V(D)) uses positive indegrees to get FG(U)=V(G) (blowup_image_eq_univ_of_full_support) and concludes from U being a proper subset, exactly as the NL's final paragraph. The supporting lemmas (blowup_boundary_product_subset, blowup_second_sdiff_subset, blowup_fst_injOn_sdiff, blowup_source_sdiff_card_le) formalize the per-block estimates (6)/(7) faithfully. Nothing is dropped, weakened, or reversed.

segments.title: Proof of Proposition 2.1
segments.reason: The segment's substantive formal content is the statement of Proposition 2.1 (the reduction), which the Lean `counterexample_reduction` captures faithfully: from an oriented counterexample `r` (IsOriented r, Counterexample r) it produces `∃ n > 0` and a graph `g` on `Fin n × Fin (n+1)` with `IsOriented g ∧ PositiveIndegree g ∧ StrictSubsetGrowth g` — exactly 'supplies the required graph G'. The proof mirrors the NL recipe: 'counterexample of minimum order and then minimum number of arcs' = `exists_minimal_counterexample`; 'Lemma 2.2 supplies positive indegrees and the subset deficit' = `hindegree` plus `subsetDeficit_of_minimal`; 'Lemma 2.3, with any integer m > |V(D)|, supplies G' = `blowup s (n+1)` with `Nat.lt_succ_self n` discharging `n = |V(D)| < n+1 = m`. Instantiating m to the specific valid value n+1 is a legitimate existence-formalization choice (the conclusion is an ∃). The leading fragment (`|U| − 2|FG(U)| + |F²G(U)| = |U| − |V(G)| < 0` for proper U) is proof detail for the strict-subset-growth inequality, and it is consistent with `StrictSubsetGrowth`'s definition `S.card + (image r (image r S)).card < 2 * (image r S).card` (i.e. |U| − 2|FG(U)| + |F²G(U)| < 0); it introduces no claim the Lean statement contradicts. Nothing is dropped, weakened, or reversed.

segments.title: Lemma 3.2 (kernels at maximum support rank) statement
segments.reason: The Lean `kernel_support` theorem captures the segment exactly. T ⊆ I × J with I, J finite is modeled by `T : Set (I × J)` with `[Fintype I] [Fintype J]`. 'Matrix supported on T' = `SupportedOn T D := ∀ s j, (s,j) ∉ T → D s j = 0` (entries outside T zero, entries in T unconstrained), matching the NL definition. 'D has maximum rank among all real matrices supported on T' = `hD : SupportedOn T D` together with `hmax : ∀ A, SupportedOn T A → A.rank ≤ D.rank`. The conclusion: for x ∈ ker D (`hx : x ∈ ker D.mulVecLin`), y ∈ ker Dᵀ (`hy : y ∈ ker Dᵀ.mulVecLin`), and (s,j) ∈ T (`hsj`), one has `x j * y s = 0`, exactly x_j y_s = 0. Indexing is consistent: s : I, j : J, x : J → ℝ, y : I → ℝ, so x_j and y_s are well-typed per the directions D : R^J → R^I and Dᵀ : R^I → R^J. Nothing dropped, weakened, or altered.

segments.title: Lemma 3.2 proof
segments.reason: The segment does two things: (1) opens the proof by contradiction, 'Suppose instead that xj ys ≠ 0' — this is faithfully matched by `by_contra hxy` giving `x j * y s ≠ 0` (and the derived `hxj : x j ≠ 0`, `hys : y s ≠ 0`); but (2) it introduces the perturbed matrix 'For a nonzero real τ, the matrix Dτ = D + τ eₛeⱼᵀ', i.e. a whole parametric family indexed by an arbitrary nonzero real τ. The Lean does NOT carry this parameter: it only ever forms `D + Matrix.single s j (1 : ℝ)`, which is the single value τ = 1 of the family. The rank-one term eₛeⱼᵀ matches `Matrix.single s j`, but the arbitrary nonzero scalar τ is dropped and hard-coded to 1, so the Lean states a special case rather than the parametric matrix the segment introduces. (The 'is still …' property the segment begins to assert is also cut off and not evaluable here.)

segments.title: Lemma 3.1 proof (augmented graph, matching, rank bound, cover)
segments.reason: This segment is the proof of Lemma 3.1 (the pruning lemma) plus the tail of the preceding argument, and the supplied Lean formalizes exactly the same proof architecture with matching quantities. (1) 'It suffices to find a vertex cover K of Γ of size at most |Z|+|H|, omitting isolated vertices' → `exists_pruning_of_augmented_cover` takes `hcover`, incidence hypotheses `hA`/`hB` (no isolated vertices in the cover), and `hbound : A.card + B.card ≤ (H).card + (Z).card`; the retention of conflict-free members and bound (8)/(9) are the `PruningResult` components `hconflictFree`, `hretainL`, `hretainR` and the final `omega` card computation (via `hTcard`, `hpartition`, `hdelL/R`, `hAsplit/Bsplit`). (2) 'a maximum matching in Γ has size at most |Z|+|H| and then giving the usual alternating-path construction of the cover [König]' → `exists_pruning_of_augmented_matching_bound` obtains a König cover of equal cardinality via `exists_vertexCover_card_eq_of_isMaximumMatching` and chains it with the matching bound; the top-level `pruning` feeds `augmented_matching_card_le_corners` (the |Z|+|H| bound, reconciled to |H|+|Z| by `Nat.add_comm`). (3) 'Each of α and β is a maximum matching in its own subgraph … augmenting path … reduces k, contradicting the choice of M' → `exists_augmented_maximum_matching` returns M maximum with `alphaEdges M`/`betaEdges M` each maximum in their R–ZR and ZL–C subgraphs (`alphaEdges_isMaximumMatching`/`betaEdges_isMaximumMatching`), and the block-respecting choice comes from `exists_maximum_matching_with_maximum_blocks` with `hblock` enforcing that right-incident augmented edges have left origin. All inequalities are ≤ in the same direction as the NL, no hypotheses are dropped or quantifiers altered, and the bound |M| = k+ℓ+t ≤ |Z|+|H| matches. The rank-encoding details (maps L,N,A,B, eqs (10)-(16), Lemma 3.2) live in the imported `AugmentedRankBound`/`MatchingAugmented` modules, i.e. 'the relevant part' shown is consistent with them. No formal claim in the segment is contradicted by the Lean.

segments.title: Proposition 4.1 (extremal contradiction) statement
segments.reason: The NL segment is the beginning of Proposition 4.1, a non-existence claim: 'There is no nonempty finite oriented graph G in which every vertex has an [...]' (the condition is cut off mid-sentence, but the assertion is clearly a statement that no such graph exists). The Lean provides two theorems: `complement_gain`, a cardinality inequality `P.card + Q.card + 2 * uncoveredCount r P Q < (leftCandidate r Q).card + (rightCandidate r P).card` about admissible pairs; and `no_strictSubsetGrowth_of_pruning`, which concludes `¬ StrictSubsetGrowth r` from `IsOriented r`, `PositiveIndegree r`, and a `PruningStatement`. Neither Lean theorem states the non-existence of a nonempty finite oriented graph characterized by a per-vertex degree/neighborhood condition; they assert internal counting/growth facts of a proof apparatus, not the proposition itself. The top-level existential/non-existence claim of the segment (∄ such graph) is not asserted by the given Lean.

segments.title: Proof of Theorem 1.1
segments.reason: The segment is proof prose describing the by-contradiction setup for Theorem 1.1: if the theorem were false, Proposition 2.1 produces a nonempty finite oriented graph with positive indegrees satisfying growth condition (17) for every nonempty proper vertex set. The Lean theorem `exists_goodVertex` states the theorem (∃ v, GoodVertex r v for oriented r), and its proof mirrors exactly this reasoning: `by_contra h` derives a `Counterexample r`, and `counterexample_reduction` yields `⟨n, hn, g, hg, hpos, hgrowth⟩` — a finite graph on `Fin n` made nonempty by `hn` (⟨0, hn⟩), `hg : IsOriented` (oriented), `hpos` (positive indegrees), and `hgrowth` (the growth/(17) condition over subsets). This correctly captures the segment's claim.
